The newest news shows how airlines, airports and government officials are working hand in hand to create a more dependable and ready-, for-the-future aviation system.

US Aviation Industry Growth Reflects a Changing Future for American Air Travel

The US Aviation Industry remains one of the most important pillars of the American transportation system, connecting communities, supporting businesses and driving tourism activity across the country. After major disruptions earlier in the decade, the sector has moved into a period focused on stability, capacity management, infrastructure improvement and long-term modernisation.

Official data from the US Department of Transportation and Bureau of Transportation Statistics shows that airline activity continues at historically significant levels, with passenger movements, flight operations and airport activity demonstrating the importance of commercial aviation in everyday life.

The industry is no longer focused only on recovering lost traffic. Instead, government agencies and aviation stakeholders are preparing for the next stage of growth. This includes upgrading airports, improving air traffic management, introducing digital systems and strengthening operational reliability.

The transformation is particularly important because aviation affects multiple sectors. Tourism depends heavily on accessible flights, businesses rely on fast connectivity, and local economies benefit from airport-driven employment and investment.

As demand patterns evolve, the US Aviation Industry Growth story is becoming closely linked with infrastructure, technology and government policy.

Passenger Demand Continues to Shape the US Aviation Industry

Millions of Travellers Keep American Skies Busy

Passenger demand remains one of the strongest forces influencing the future direction of aviation in the United States.

According to Bureau of Transportation Statistics data, US airlines continue carrying hundreds of millions of passengers annually through domestic and international networks. Recent BTS reporting shows significant passenger volumes moving through American carriers, highlighting the continued importance of air travel in national mobility.

Domestic aviation remains especially important because the United States has one of the world’s largest internal air travel markets. Thousands of daily flights connect major cities, regional communities and smaller destinations.

International connectivity is also a major economic driver. Airports serving gateway cities continue handling travellers arriving for tourism, education, trade and business activities.

The continued demand for flights has encouraged airlines and airports to rethink how they manage capacity. Instead of simply adding more flights, operators are increasingly focusing on efficiency, schedule reliability and improved passenger experiences.

This shift represents a broader change in the aviation industry. Growth is now measured not only by passenger numbers but also by service quality, operational performance and infrastructure capability.

Government Data Shows the Scale of America’s Aviation Network

BTS Statistics Provide Insight Into Airline Operations

The Bureau of Transportation Statistics plays a central role in monitoring the performance of the American transportation system.

Its aviation databases track airline passenger traffic, flight activity, fares, delays, employment and operational performance. These statistics provide government agencies, industry professionals and travellers with a clearer understanding of how the aviation system operates.

Recent BTS aviation reporting highlights continued large-scale activity across US airlines, with scheduled carriers operating extensive networks connecting hundreds of airports.

The data also shows that aviation performance depends on multiple factors, including weather conditions, airport capacity, aircraft availability and air traffic management.

For travellers, these statistics help explain why some periods experience increased delays or schedule pressure. For policymakers, the information supports decisions about infrastructure investment and regulatory improvements.

The importance of reliable aviation data has increased as the industry becomes more complex. Modern air travel involves millions of daily interactions between airlines, airports, passengers and government systems.

Through continuous monitoring, agencies can identify challenges and develop policies aimed at improving safety and efficiency.

FAA Modernisation Efforts Transform the Future of US Air Travel

Technology Investment Becomes a Key Aviation Priority

The Federal Aviation Administration continues to focus on modernising the systems that support American aviation.

One of the biggest priorities is improving air traffic management technology. The FAA manages one of the world’s busiest aviation environments, handling tens of thousands of flights every day across the National Airspace System.

Modernisation programmes aim to replace ageing systems, improve communication networks and increase efficiency across air traffic operations.

The FAA has also highlighted the importance of advanced technology, better data systems and improved coordination between airports and aviation operators.

These improvements are essential because future aviation growth will require more than additional aircraft. The entire system must be capable of handling increasing demand safely.

Modern air traffic technology can help reduce congestion, improve routing efficiency and support more predictable travel experiences.

The development of a smarter aviation network is expected to remain a major priority as the US Aviation Industry prepares for future expansion.

Airports Become Major Growth Engines for the US Aviation Industry

The future of the US Aviation Industry depends heavily on modern airports capable of handling increasing passenger demand, improving efficiency and delivering better traveller experiences. Across the United States, airport authorities are investing in terminals, runways, taxiways, security systems and passenger facilities to support the next phase of aviation growth.

The Federal Aviation Administration continues to support airport development through major infrastructure programmes designed to improve safety, capacity and reliability. FAA airport grant programmes provide funding for critical projects, including runway improvements, taxiway upgrades, airport lighting systems and other essential infrastructure needs.

Airport development has become a central part of the national aviation strategy because airports are more than transportation facilities. They are economic centres that support employment, tourism, trade and regional development.

Large international airports are expanding their capacity to manage higher passenger volumes, while smaller regional airports are receiving support to improve connectivity and maintain essential air services.

The changing airport landscape reflects a broader transformation. Travellers increasingly expect faster processing, digital services, comfortable facilities and reliable connections. As a result, infrastructure investment is becoming a key factor in maintaining the competitiveness of the US Aviation Industry.

Federal Infrastructure Programmes Strengthen American Airports

Government Funding Supports Long-Term Aviation Development

Federal investment has become a major driver of airport improvement across the United States.

Through infrastructure programmes administered by the FAA, airports nationwide are receiving support for projects designed to improve operational safety, increase capacity and modernise passenger facilities. The FAA’s Airport Improvement Program provides grants for public-use airports included in the National Plan of Integrated Airport Systems.

These investments cover a wide range of projects, including:

Runway rehabilitation

Taxiway improvements

Terminal development

Safety equipment upgrades

Airfield improvements

Accessibility enhancements

The focus is not only on expanding airport size but also on improving efficiency. Modern airports require advanced systems that allow passengers, airlines and airport operators to move more smoothly through the travel process.

The FAA has also supported airport terminal improvements through infrastructure funding initiatives, helping airports upgrade ageing facilities and create more efficient passenger environments.

For communities across America, airport investment provides wider economic benefits. Construction projects create jobs, while improved connectivity helps businesses attract investment and enables tourism growth.

Air Traffic Control Modernisation Becomes a National Aviation Priority

FAA Technology Upgrades Aim to Improve Efficiency and Reliability

One of the biggest challenges facing the US Aviation Industry is modernising the systems that manage one of the world’s busiest airspaces.

The FAA is undertaking major efforts to upgrade air traffic control infrastructure, replacing older technology with modern digital systems designed to improve reliability and efficiency. Recent government-backed modernisation plans focus on improving communications, surveillance systems and operational coordination.

The FAA has identified ageing infrastructure as a key area requiring investment as aviation demand continues to evolve. Modern air traffic systems are expected to support safer operations, reduce inefficiencies and help manage future growth.

Government officials have highlighted the need to accelerate upgrades to critical aviation technology, including communication networks and radar infrastructure.

The modernisation effort is significant because air traffic management affects every part of the aviation ecosystem. Airlines depend on efficient routing, airports rely on predictable operations, and passengers benefit from improved schedule reliability.

As aircraft movements increase, advanced technology will become increasingly important in maintaining the performance of the national airspace system.

Airline Innovation Reshapes Passenger Experience Across America

Digital Services and Operational Improvements Drive Competition

While infrastructure remains essential, airlines are also transforming how passengers experience air travel.

The modern US Aviation Industry is increasingly focused on improving customer service through digital tools, personalised experiences and operational efficiency.

Airlines are investing in:

Mobile applications

Digital boarding solutions

Real-time travel updates

Automated customer services

Improved onboard experiences

Technology has become a major factor in how travellers interact with airlines. Passengers now expect immediate information about schedules, gate changes, baggage updates and travel disruptions.

The shift towards digital aviation is also helping airlines manage operations more effectively. Better data systems allow carriers to analyse demand patterns, optimise schedules and respond faster during disruptions.

However, technology alone cannot solve every challenge. Aviation remains dependent on coordination between airlines, airports, air traffic authorities and government agencies.

The future of airline innovation will likely involve balancing digital transformation with operational reliability, safety standards and customer expectations.

Tourism and Business Growth Depend on Strong Air Connectivity

Aviation Remains a Foundation of the American Economy

The importance of the US Aviation Industry extends far beyond airlines and airports.

Air connectivity plays a major role in supporting tourism, international business, trade and local economic development.

Millions of visitors arrive in the United States each year for holidays, conferences, education and business activities. Reliable aviation networks allow destinations across the country to benefit from international and domestic visitors.

Major airport hubs connect global markets with American cities, while regional airports provide essential links for smaller communities.

The aviation sector also supports a wide range of jobs, including:

Airline employees

Airport workers

Aviation maintenance specialists

Security personnel

Technology providers

Tourism professionals

Strong air connectivity helps businesses reach customers, attract investment and participate in global markets.

As travel demand continues evolving, aviation infrastructure will remain closely connected with economic performance.

Sustainability Becomes a Key Direction for Future Aviation Growth

Government and Industry Focus on Cleaner Aviation Solutions

The next phase of the US Aviation Industry will also be shaped by sustainability goals and environmental innovation.

Government agencies and aviation stakeholders are exploring ways to reduce emissions while maintaining the benefits of air connectivity.

Important areas of development include:

Sustainable aviation fuel

More efficient aircraft technology

Improved air traffic management

Airport energy improvements

Operational efficiency measures

Cleaner aviation technologies are expected to play an increasingly important role as the industry balances growth with environmental responsibilities.

Air traffic efficiency also contributes to sustainability. More efficient flight routes and improved operational planning can help reduce unnecessary fuel consumption.

The challenge for policymakers and aviation companies is creating solutions that support both economic growth and environmental objectives.

Regional Airports Gain Importance in Expanding Aviation Networks

Smaller Communities Benefit From Improved Connectivity

While major international airports receive significant attention, regional airports remain an important part of the American aviation system.

Many smaller communities depend on air services for economic connections, healthcare access, tourism and business development.

Government programmes support regional aviation by improving airport infrastructure and maintaining connectivity opportunities.

Regional airports also help reduce pressure on larger hubs by providing alternative travel options and supporting distributed aviation networks.

For travellers, stronger regional connectivity can create easier access to destinations beyond major metropolitan areas.

For local economies, airport improvements can attract businesses and encourage tourism investment.

The continued development of regional aviation demonstrates that future growth will not only come from large airport expansions but also from strengthening connections throughout the country.

The Economic Impact of the US Aviation Industry Continues to Expand

Aviation Remains a Strategic National Asset

The US Aviation Industry contributes significantly to economic activity by supporting transportation, tourism and commerce.

Airports act as economic centres, generating employment and encouraging surrounding development. Airlines support domestic mobility, while international routes strengthen America’s connection with global markets.

Government aviation policies increasingly recognise the importance of maintaining a reliable and competitive transportation network.

Investment in aviation infrastructure creates benefits beyond immediate construction projects. Better airports and improved air traffic systems can support long-term economic growth.

The aviation sector also plays a critical role during periods of increased travel demand, helping businesses and communities remain connected.

As the industry enters its next phase, maintaining strong infrastructure and efficient operations will remain essential.

Future Outlook for the US Aviation Industry

Growth Will Depend on Technology, Infrastructure and Passenger Needs

The future of the US Aviation Industry will be shaped by three major priorities: modern infrastructure, advanced technology and changing traveller expectations.

Passenger demand is expected to remain a central driver of aviation planning. As more people rely on air travel, airports and airlines will need to continue improving capacity and efficiency.

Government agencies will remain focused on safety, modernisation and investment programmes that support long-term aviation development.

Future aviation growth will depend on:

Smarter airports

More efficient air traffic management

Better passenger services

Stronger regional connectivity

Sustainable aviation solutions

The industry’s transformation is not limited to increasing flight numbers. It represents a broader shift towards creating a more connected, efficient and resilient aviation system.

The next generation of American aviation will be defined by how successfully airlines, airports and government agencies work together to meet future demand.

Conclusion

US Aviation Industry stepping into a phase. This new phase is shaped by passenger demand, advanced technology, airport investment and governmental modernisation efforts. Official aviation programmes show that improving infrastructure, safety systems and operational efficiency will remain essential for supporting growth. As airlines and airports adapt to changing traveller expectations the sector continues to strengthen its role in tourism, business and economic development. The future of the US Aviation Industry will depend on collaboration between regulators, carriers and communities to create a reliable, sustainable and connected transportation network for millions of travellers, across the United States driven again by passenger demand.

title: OMV Petrom invests 115 million euros in Petrobrazi - Inspenet
description:
OMV Petrom has invested approximately €115 million (US$133.5 million) in modernizing the electrical infrastructure of the Petrobrazi refinery in Romania.
OMV Petrom modernizes Petrobrazi's electrical infrastructure Specifically, the project included the construction of a high-voltage power line directly connected to the Transelectrica substation.
Furthermore, the electrical infrastructure takes on special relevance in light of the projects that OMV Petrom is developing within Petrobrazi.
Green hydrogen is part of OMV Petrom's plans Furthermore, OMV Petrom is developing green hydrogen production capabilities at Petrobrazi.
Petrobrazi's transformation is progressing with new investments Finally, the 115 million euros allocated to electrical infrastructure are part of a broader industrial program.
text:
OMV Petrom has invested approximately €115 million (US$133.5 million) in modernizing the electrical infrastructure of the Petrobrazi refinery in Romania. The project is part of the transformation program the company is undertaking at this industrial complex.

With this investment, the company aims to strengthen the electricity supply necessary to maintain Petrobrazi's current operations. In turn, the new infrastructure will allow for the incorporation of production capacities currently under development at the refinery.

These include projects aimed at producing sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO), and green hydrogen. These initiatives are part of OMV Petrom's plans to adapt its operations to the evolving needs of the energy market.

OMV Petrom modernizes Petrobrazi's electrical infrastructure

Specifically, the project included the construction of a high-voltage power line directly connected to the Transelectrica substation. It also included a new-generation electrical substation and another facility designed to distribute power within the complex.

OMV Petrom also incorporated Blue GIS technology into the new infrastructure; it is an electrical switching system designed to offer a lower environmental impact.

The modernization will provide a network prepared to meet the consumption needs of both the existing facilities and the units that will be incorporated during the transformation of Petrobrazi.

According to Radu Căprău, OMV Petrom's executive board member responsible for Refining and Marketing, having a modern electrical infrastructure is essential for the proper functioning of a refinery.

The executive also noted that the investment will support current operations and new capabilities related to SAF, HVO and green hydrogen.

Petrobrazi is preparing to produce SAF and renewable diesel.

Furthermore, the electrical infrastructure takes on special relevance in light of the projects that OMV Petrom is developing within Petrobrazi.

The company began construction in 2025 of a unit to produce SAF and HVO at the refinery. According to the plans announced by the company, these facilities will have a combined capacity of approximately 250,000 tons per year.

Commercial production is planned to begin in 2028. The project will allow Petrobrazi to expand its activity towards fuels intended for sectors where reducing emissions presents greater difficulties, including aviation.

In this context, the SAF will be especially important for air transport. Meanwhile, the HVO will allow for the production of renewable diesel through the processing of bio-based raw materials.

The availability of a higher-capacity electrical infrastructure facilitates the integration of these units into the overall operation of the refinery.

Green hydrogen is part of OMV Petrom's plans

Furthermore, OMV Petrom is developing green hydrogen production capabilities at Petrobrazi. This fuel will play a direct role in the processes associated with the production of fuels with a lower carbon footprint.

The company is thus working on various projects that are gradually modifying the refinery's production profile. The new electrical infrastructure provides a foundation for supplying power to these facilities and facilitating their integration with existing units.

The commitment to green hydrogen complements the planned production of SAF and HVO. Together, these projects demonstrate how OMV Petrom is directing part of its investments toward new energy sources and fuels as part of its energy transition strategy.

A 7 MW photovoltaic project will expand the electricity supply

7 megawatt (MW) photovoltaic project is being built within Petrobrazi.

Currently, the refinery has its own power generation unit, which covers virtually all of its electricity needs. The addition of solar capacity will expand the available energy sources within the complex.

In this way, Petrobrazi will combine its own generation capacity with a renewed electrical infrastructure and a high-voltage connection. This configuration will facilitate the necessary supply for the industrial projects that OMV Petrom has underway.

Petrobrazi maintains a relevant role in the Romanian market

Petrobrazi is one of OMV Petrom's main industrial assets in Romania; the refinery has a processing capacity of approximately 4.5 million tons of crude oil per year.

Furthermore, its operations have a considerable impact on the supply of fuels and other petroleum products to the Romanian market.

Since 2005, OMV Petrom has invested over €2 billion in the modernization of Petrobrazi. These investments have enabled the upgrading of existing facilities and prepared the refinery to incorporate new technologies and production lines.

Petrobrazi's transformation is progressing with new investments

Finally, the 115 million euros allocated to electrical infrastructure are part of a broader industrial program.

green hydrogen projects and new photovoltaic capacity show the different areas in which OMV Petrom is involved in Petrobrazi.

With these actions, the company seeks to maintain the refinery's operational capacity while adapting part of its production to the changes resulting from the energy transition.

The new electricity grid will play a cross-cutting role in this process. Its capacity will allow for the connection of projects requiring a stable supply and will facilitate Petrobrazi's gradual incorporation of new forms of energy production.

News of additional interest

DNV and Fassmer make progress on autonomous naval vessels

DNV and the German shipbuilder Fassmer have signed an agreement to collaborate on the development and classification of autonomous and remotely operated vessels for naval and government clients. The work will apply DNV's AROS standards to Fassmer's unmanned projects and will examine areas such as navigation, engineering, operations, and safety.

The collaboration includes evaluating new technologies and defining pathways for certifying these vessels. The companies will seek to advance toward possible Approval in Principle under the AROS framework. These standards, available since 2025, cover everything from remotely controlled vessels to fully autonomous systems. DNV and Fassmer also expect to contribute their findings to the development of international standards for this sector.

Energy Vault secures 275 MW for AI centers

Energy Vault secured 275 MW of power generation capacity with Rolls-Royce MTU engines to support large artificial intelligence and high-performance computing campuses. The equipment will be delivered between the second half of 2027 and the first half of 2028. The company also obtained financing from Eagle Point Credit Management to cover the acquisition without using large amounts of corporate capital before allocating it to projects.

The generators will be part of Powered Land, Energy Vault's platform for delivering power directly to data center sites. The company plans to combine this generation with batteries, electrical systems, and advanced controls. The 275 MW will support discussions for multi-gigawatt projects and can be deployed gradually as the needs of each campus increase.

US searches for hidden geothermal energy using algorithms

The U.S. Department of Energy announced $300,000 for the GEMS Award , a competition that seeks to improve the detection of geothermal resources hidden underground. Participants will be required to develop and test algorithms capable of analyzing geophysical data and identifying faults and other structures related to potential geothermal energy deposits.

The competition will have two rounds with prizes ranging from $15,000 to $100,000 and will accept proposals until December 3, 2026. The models will work with real data to generate more accurate geological maps. The government hopes these tools will reduce uncertainty during exploration and facilitate the discovery of commercially viable resources.

Anthropic proposes to put a stop to the advance of AI

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has proposed slowing the pace at which the capabilities of advanced artificial intelligence models are increasing. His proposals include incorporating external evaluators within companies to test their security measures and review potential incidents. Anthropic has pledged to allow this type of oversight and has called on other leading companies to do the same.

Amodei also proposes that large companies agree on common standards to control the development of advanced models with the support of the U.S. government. Internationally, he suggests seeking agreements with China and other countries to limit uses considered dangerous, such as the creation of biological weapons. At the same time, he advocates for restrictions on chips and technology to maintain the United States' advantage over Chinese development.

text:
Shanghai, China, 7 September 2026 – Axens and Wison Engineering signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to explore collaboration opportunities on global Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and eSAF projects, including the Fischer-Tropsch pathway. Through this framework, the two companies will jointly assess practical execution approaches that combine Axens’ proven process technology expertise and Wison Engineering’s capabilities in standardization, modularization, global supply-chain integration and international project execution. The objective is to develop eSAF solutions designed for greater cost and schedule predictability, rapid deployment and efficient replication across global markets.

Axens is a leading international provider of process technologies, developed by IFP Energies Nouvelles (IFPEN), catalysts, equipment and services for the energy transition, refining, chemicals and gas industries. The company offers a broad portfolio of low-carbon solutions, including Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF).

Wison Engineering is a leading provider of EPC services and integrated technology solutions for the energy and chemical industries. Established in 1997 and listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (stock code: 02236.HK) in 2012, the company specializes in oil & gas processing, petrochemicals, C1 chemicals, new energy, and other sectors. text:
ROMA – La crisi energetica dovuta alle prolungate tensioni internazionali in Medio Oriente è ormai giunta a un nodo cruciale. Prima dell’attacco congiunto di Stati Uniti e Israele all’Iran, nello Stretto di Hormuz transitavano circa 21 milioni di barili di greggio al giorno, quasi il 20% della produzione petrolifera globale. In queste settimane, secondo i dati dell’Agenzia internazionale dell’Energia (Aie), questi numeri sono più che dimezzati a causa della chiusura prolungata dell’unico sbocco marittimo del Golfo Persico.

Crisi energetica e caro carburanti, il peso delle tensioni internazionali

L’altro collo di bottiglia è rappresentato dallo Stretto di Bab al-Mandab, tra Yemen e Corno d’Africa, viadotto fondamentale per le imbarcazioni che dal Golfo di Aden risalgono in mar Rosso in direzione del Canale di Suez. Quest’area, attualmente sotto il controllo dei ribelli yemeniti Houthi, rischia di essere soggetta anch’essa a restrizioni che potrebbero gravemente condizionare le rotte commerciali.

Il petrolio non giungerebbe dunque a destinazione in tempi più brevi, provocando un aggravio dei consumi per le navi, un’impennata dei costi per l’intera filiera e, di riflesso, per i cittadini. Così, l’Europa rischia di essere ancora una volta una delle vittime principali. Il conto è presentato dai forti rincari sul carburante che si mantengono ormai da sei mesi. Da giorni benzina e diesel hanno superato il prezzo dei 2 euro a litro, una ‘soglia psicologica’ che non veniva toccata dalla metà di settembre 2023 a causa dello shock energetico provocato dalla guerra in Ucraina e dal taglio della produzione di petrolio da parte dei Paesi dell’Opec.

Biocarburanti, la risposta alla sicurezza energetica europea

Secondo lo studio “Sustainable biofuels as a strategic lever for industrial competitiveness, energy security and decarbonization” condotto da Teha Group ed Eni e presentato lo scorso 5 settembre nell’ambito del Forum di Cernobbio (Como), l’impatto della crisi dello Stretto di Hormuz nel 2026 sul Pil dell’Unione europea è stato di 36 miliardi di euro. Un aggravio che rappresenta un nervo scoperto in tema di sicurezza energetica e decarbonizzazione per il Vecchio Continente.

In questo quadro, risulta fondamentale riuscire a garantire, sottolinea lo studio, “catene di approvvigionamento diversificate e resilienti”. Ora, nel corso di questi anni l’Europa ha avuto un approccio decisamente tiepido nei confronti dei cosiddetti “biocarburanti da materie prime rinnovabili” come l’Hvo (Hydrogenated vegetable oil) e il Saf (Sustainable aviation fuel).

Hvo e Saf, la crescita dei biocarburanti nel mondo

Analizzando la domanda globale di biocarburanti nel decennio 2015-2025, si scopre come tale indice sia in netto incremento, con il Nord America e l’America Latina ai primi posti. L’Europa, invece, si posiziona decisamente indietro anche a causa di normative stringenti. Dando uno sguardo solo all’ultimo anno, nel 2025 il Nord America è stato coinvolto con quote del 39% nel mercato globale dei biocarburanti, mentre l’America Latina ha toccato il 25% delle quote. L’Europa si è fatta avanti con appena il 16%, superata perfino dall’Asia, con il 20% delle richieste.

Insomma, il ritardo è notevole, se si considera che, secondo le previsioni di Thea Group su dati Aie, la domanda a livello globale di biocarburanti liquidi è destinata a crescere nei prossimi decenni, con un incremento stimato tra il minimo del +42% e il massimo dell’84% entro il 2050. Inoltre, tale dinamica potrebbe avere una condotta sorprendente già nel breve periodo, poiché “lo scenario a maggiore crescita – si legge nel rapporto – realizza il 75% della crescita aggiuntiva entro il 2035, accelerando la decarbonizzazione dei trasporti”.

Europa, Stati Uniti e Cina: la competizione sui biocarburanti

Tra i principali competitor dell’Ue a livello globale vi sono Brasile, Cina e Stati Uniti. Queste tre grandi economie hanno sviluppato dei metodi differenti rispetto al Vecchio Continente integrando, sottolinea il report, “strumenti di sicurezza energetica, sviluppo agricolo e competitività delle esportazioni. L’Unione, invece, è l’unica realtà economica “a combinare criteri di sostenibilità vincolanti, restrizioni sulle materie prime e obiettivi di consumo stringenti”.

L’espansione dei biocarburanti in Europa è stato inoltre limitato in questi anni da numerosi pregiudizi privi di fondamento scientifico, oltre che da una corsa spasmodica in direzione pressoché esclusiva dei motori elettrici. Per tanto tempo è stato detto che i biocarburanti non possono essere concepiti come una soluzione chiave per favorire la transizione ecologica. Tuttavia, le “nuove generazioni” di prodotti creati da materia prima di origine naturale hanno superato tale preconcetto, emergendo come “sostituti pienamente compatibili, utilizzabili fino al 100% di purezza”. Inoltre, i moderni biocarburanti possono essere già utilizzati in buona dei veicoli già esistenti.

Biocarburanti e motori tradizionali, quali veicoli sono compatibili

In Europa, per esempio, oltre 170 milioni di veicoli a diesel Euro 5-V ed Euro 6-VI – pari al 60% dell’intero parco auto circolante) risulta essere già compatibile con questa tipologia di carburanti, previa autorizzazione del costruttore. Buone notizie potrebbero presto arrivare anche per i possessori di veicoli a benzina e per altri mezzi con motori a combustione interna. E ancora, il diesel Hvo può essere impiegato anche per i motori marini senza modifiche, così come il Sustainable aviation fuel (Saf) può essere utilizzato per miscele fino al 50% nel trasporto aereo.

Hvo, quanto costa il biocarburante rispetto all’auto elettrica

E i costi? Secondo un’analisi di Transport & Environment (T&E), organizzazione indipendente, apartitica e senza scopo di lucro che promuove la decarbonizzazione dei trasporti in Europa entro il 2050, l’utilizzo dell’Hvo – il biocarburante più innovativo attualmente sul mercato – comporta un costo medio per un consumatore europeo superiore del 79% rispetto alla ricarica di un’auto elettrica.

In base ai calcoli, una ricarica costa in media circa 7 euro ogni 100 km, mentre per percorrere la stessa distanza usufruendo dell’Hvo puro si spendono fino a 13 euro. Tuttavia, un altro paragone da prendere in considerazione è quello con i carburanti fossili, ovvero benzina e diesel, che potrebbero già essere ampiamente sostituiti con un prodotto decisamente meno inquinante (-80% delle emissioni di gas serra, con possibilità di emissioni nulle o negative, con una rimozione di Co2 maggiore di quanta ne emettano, fino a -114% per Hvo e fino a -33% per il Saf) e già, come detto, disponibile, considerato che la sostituzione dei mezzi tradizionali con quelli elettrici procede molto lentamente anche per via dei costi, ancora per molte famiglie proibitivi.

Hvo e benzina, il confronto sui costi

Inoltre, utilizzare un biocarburante in luogo della benzina comporterebbe già un risparmio, seppur minimo. Secondo il prezzo medio settimanale rilevato dal Mase (dato aggiornato al 14 settembre 2026), per percorrere 100 km è necessario spendere 14,53 euro. Inoltre, i biocarburanti riescono a resistere meglio alla volatilità dei prezzi alla pompa. Come sottolineato ancora da Teha, durante la crisi dello Stretto di Hormuz i prezzi di riferimento del mercato del diesel sono aumentati del 79% nel periodo tra febbraio e agosto 2026, mentre l’Hvo ha conosciuto un incremento soltanto del 10%.

In sintesi, i biocarburanti non devono essere considerati una “soluzione unica”, in particolare modo al posto dell’elettrico, ma rappresentano comunque un buon ponte tra l’era dei combustibili fossili e il futuro green.

La bioraffinazione passa anche dalla Sicilia. Gela e Priolo le pioniere della riconversione

Dal 2009 l’Europa ha perso il 21% della propria capacità primaria di raffinazione, con la conseguente chiusura di 30 impianti su 102 e una perdita stimata tra 90 mila e 130 mila posti di lavoro qualificati. Si tratta del dato che emerge dallo studio strategico realizzato da Teha Group in collaborazione con Eni presentato al Forum di Cernobbio 2026 e che pone l’accento sulle principali sfide del Vecchio Continente in tema di competitività industriale e decarbonizzazione. Di contro, però, non è calata la domanda di diesel e jet fuel, per i quali l’Europa continua a essere estremamente dipendenti dalle importazioni.

Il futuro, però, non aspetta l’Ue poiché, come abbiamo scritto in precedenza, altre aree del globo stanno compiendo passi da gigante verso l’indipendenza da combustibili fossili. L’Europa, culla della rivoluzione industriale, si trova adesso costretta a riconvertire quelle aree altrimenti destinate al declino attraverso dei programmi che mirano non solo a valorizzare i siti esistenti, ma anche a preservare i posti di lavoro e garantire livelli soddisfacenti di salvaguardia ambientale. Francia e Germania sono tra i più fulgidi esempi in tema di riconversione delle vecchie raffinerie in moderne bioraffinerie.

In Italia la politica della bioraffinazione è partita nel 2014 da Porto Marghera, a Venezia, con la conversione targata Eni della vecchia raffineria in bioraffineria per la produzione di biocarburanti. Sempre nello stesso periodo, l’azienda ha firmato un protocollo d’intesa presso il Ministero dello Sviluppo economico con le organizzazioni sindacali, le Istituzioni e Confindustria per il rilancio dell’area di Gela, avviando così il processo di conversione dei vecchi impianti in bioraffineria, definita dalla stessa Eni come “la più all’avanguardia d’Europa”.

L’infrastruttura produce oggi biocarburante Hvo derivato al 100% da materie prime rinnovabili. Inoltre, sempre a Gela vengono prodotti carburanti Saf per l’aviazione, i cui bio-componenti trattati – sottolinea Eni, “danno origine a biojet, un carburante miscelabile con il prodotto convenzionale”.

L’altro grande impianto siciliano di bioraffinazione è quello di Priolo Gargallo, in provincia di Siracusa. A inizio febbraio 2026 Eni ha annunciato “un importante investimento strategico” in sinergia con Q8 che consentirà di convertire scarti e residui di oli vegetali “in biocarburanti utilizzabili anche in purezza al 100%”.

text:
ANA has been making strides towards sustainable travel through innovation in Sustainable Aviation Fuel and other environmentally friendly ways of traveling. ANA or All Nippon Airways has increased its commitment towards sustainable travel through emphasis on Sustainable Aviation Fuel and eco-friendly aviation. With the continuous growth of tourism in the world, the airline company aims to make air travel a sustainable mode of transport while retaining its international connections. ANA has developed a plan for reaching zero net carbon emissions through its aircraft operations by 2050, and SAF will be one of its most critical strategies.

The airline’s sustainability approach comes at a time when aviation is facing increasing pressure to reduce emissions while meeting rising passenger demand. Through fuel innovation, operational improvements and passenger awareness initiatives, ANA is creating a model where future travel can combine convenience, technology and environmental responsibility.

Sustainable Aviation Fuel Becomes The Core Of ANA Green Travel Strategy

At the centre of ANA’s sustainability roadmap is Sustainable Aviation Fuel, a next-generation fuel designed to reduce lifecycle carbon emissions compared with conventional jet fuel. SAF can be produced from renewable resources including waste materials, used cooking oil and other sustainable feedstocks, helping airlines reduce their dependence on traditional fossil-based aviation fuel.

ANA has committed to increasing SAF usage across its operations, targeting the replacement of at least 10% of its jet fuel consumption with SAF by fiscal year 2030. The airline is also working with industry partners and stakeholders to support the development of stable SAF supply chains, particularly in Japan.

The adoption of SAF represents a major shift in the aviation sector because it allows existing aircraft infrastructure to continue operating while reducing environmental impact. Unlike completely new aircraft technologies that may require decades of development, SAF can be introduced into current aviation systems through approved fuel blending methods.

ANA Future Promise Programme Supports Responsible Travel Experiences

ANA’s sustainability efforts are organised under initiatives such as the ANA Future Promise programme, which focuses on reducing environmental impacts across different areas of airline operations.

The programme supports several sustainability goals, including:

Increasing the use of Sustainable Aviation Fuel

Reducing carbon emissions from flight operations

Improving resource efficiency

Reducing waste

Creating more sustainable onboard services

Promoting environmental awareness among passengers

Through these efforts, ANA aims to make sustainability part of the complete travel journey rather than limiting it only to aircraft operations.

Green Pokémon Jet Adds A New Dimension To ANA Passenger Experience

The launch of the Green Pokémon Jet highlights another side of ANA’s travel innovation strategy by combining aviation, entertainment and memorable passenger experiences.

The aircraft was unveiled during a special event before beginning its first flight from Tokyo Haneda Airport to Honolulu at 9:55 p.m. The aircraft features a dedicated Pokémon design, bringing the popular franchise into the travel experience from the aircraft exterior to the cabin environment.

Passengers travelling on the Green Pokémon Jet can experience several Pokémon-themed features, including:

Special Pokémon headrest covers

Pokémon-designed paper cups

Custom napkins

Pokémon plush toys onboard

Background music featuring Pokémon themes

Pokémon-focused inflight entertainment

The entertainment selection includes “Pokémon: The First Movie” and “Pokémon TV Anime Theme Songs BEST OF BEST OF BEST 1997–2023 Disc 1”, creating a themed journey for families, fans and leisure travellers.

While the Green Pokémon Jet focuses on entertainment and customer experience, it reflects ANA’s wider approach of creating innovative travel concepts while continuing its environmental commitments.

ANA Moves Towards Net Zero Aviation By 2050

ANA has set a target to achieve net-zero carbon emissions from aircraft operations by 2050. The airline’s pathway includes multiple solutions, with SAF serving as a central component of its decarbonisation strategy.

The airline’s environmental roadmap includes:

ANA recognises that achieving a cleaner aviation future requires cooperation across airlines, fuel producers, governments and technology companies. The airline has also worked with other aviation stakeholders to highlight the importance of expanding SAF production and improving accessibility.

More Efficient Flight Operations Help Reduce Aviation Emissions

Alongside SAF investment, ANA is improving aircraft operations to lower fuel consumption and emissions.

The airline is focusing on:

Optimised flight planning

Improved fuel management

Operational efficiency

Advanced navigation techniques

Better use of aircraft technology

These measures allow airlines to reduce environmental impact while continuing to provide global air connectivity.

ANA’s sustainability approach recognises that green aviation cannot depend on a single solution. Instead, a combination of cleaner fuels, efficient operations and future technologies will be needed to support the transition towards low-carbon travel.

Sustainable Onboard Services Create A Greener Passenger Journey

ANA is also working to make the passenger experience more sustainable through improvements in onboard materials and services.

The airline has introduced environmental initiatives connected with cabin operations, including efforts to reduce waste and explore alternative materials. ANA’s sustainability-focused aircraft programmes have included environmentally designed cabin elements, showing how small details within the passenger journey can contribute to wider environmental goals.

From fuel choices to onboard services, ANA is gradually transforming different stages of air travel into more environmentally conscious experiences.

ANA Strengthens The Future Of Green Tourism

The growth of sustainable travel is becoming increasingly important for the global tourism industry. Travellers are looking beyond destinations and increasingly considering how their journeys are created, including the environmental impact of transportation.

By investing in Sustainable Aviation Fuel, operational efficiency and innovative passenger experiences, ANA is supporting the evolution of green travel. The airline’s approach demonstrates how aviation companies are working to balance tourism growth with climate responsibility.

The Green Pokémon Jet represents the creative side of this transformation, connecting aviation with entertainment and cultural experiences, while ANA’s SAF strategy represents the technical foundation behind a more sustainable future.

ANA has been driving forward the development of green transportation by creating innovative Sustainable Aviation Fuels, cleaner operations, and a sustainable future for aviation.

With the rapid growth of international travel, it is clear that the new trend in the global aviation sector is that of moving towards a sustainable future through innovation and efficiency.

text:
Listrik Indonesia | Program mandatori biodiesel 50% atau B50 yang mulai berlaku pada Juli 2026 dipastikan tetap dilanjutkan pada 2027. Pemerintah kini memanfaatkan masa penerapan awal tersebut untuk memastikan pasokan bahan baku, kesiapan produsen, infrastruktur, hingga distribusi biodiesel dapat berjalan tanpa kendala.

Direktur Jenderal Energi Baru, Terbarukan, dan Konservasi Energi (EBTKE) Kementerian ESDM Eniya Listiani Dewi mengatakan, keberhasilan B50 tidak hanya ditentukan oleh kemampuan produksi biodiesel. Kepastian pasokan bahan baku, investasi produsen, serta kesiapan rantai logistik menjadi faktor penting yang perlu dijaga agar penyaluran B50 di pasar berjalan sesuai target.

“Target B50 ini ditargetkan tetap untuk tahun 2027. Kami ingin memastikan komitmen penyaluran B50 di pasar berjalan tanpa kendala, sehingga dibutuhkan kolaborasi erat dengan seluruh rantai pasok dan pengiriman guna mendorong investasi serta pemenuhan volume,” ujar Eniya dalam sambutan secara daring pada 6th Palm Biodiesel Conference 2026 di Nusa Dua, Bali, Kamis (17/9/2026).

Menurut Eniya, penerapan B50 membutuhkan kesiapan dari seluruh mata rantai industri. Mulai dari ketersediaan bahan baku, kemampuan produksi, hingga pengiriman kepada pengguna akhir harus berjalan selaras. Hal ini penting karena peningkatan kadar biodiesel turut meningkatkan kebutuhan terhadap kapasitas produksi dan kelancaran distribusi.

Pemerintah juga perlu memastikan pasokan tetap tersedia seiring dengan berlanjutnya program pada 2027. Kepastian volume menjadi salah satu kunci agar implementasi B50 dapat berlangsung secara konsisten dan tidak terganggu persoalan logistik maupun keterbatasan pasokan.

Bagi industri biodiesel, keberlanjutan program tersebut memberikan kepastian dalam menyusun rencana produksi dan investasi. Produsen memiliki ruang untuk memperkuat kapasitas sekaligus menyesuaikan rantai pasok dengan kebutuhan biodiesel yang semakin besar.

B60 Masih Hadapi Tantangan Teknis

Setelah B50, pembahasan mengenai peningkatan kadar campuran biodiesel juga mulai mengarah pada skenario B60. Namun, Eniya menyebut penerapan campuran hingga 60% masih menghadapi tantangan, khususnya jika tambahan campuran seluruhnya mengandalkan Fatty Acid Methyl Ester (FAME).

Salah satu opsi yang tengah diperhitungkan adalah penggunaan Hydrotreated Vegetable Oil (HVO) untuk mengisi tambahan porsi campuran tersebut. Dengan skema ini, tambahan 10% menuju B60 berpotensi berasal dari HVO.

“Pencampuran hingga 60% memiliki tantangan tersendiri. Namun, ada potensi kita menambah 10% menggunakan HVO jika ingin melampaui B50, dengan catatan tetap mempertimbangkan keekonomian dan penyesuaian harga HVO di pasar,” jelasnya.

Dengan demikian, peningkatan menuju B60 tidak semata-mata persoalan menaikkan persentase campuran. Ketersediaan HVO, teknologi, kapasitas produksi, serta harga produk menjadi sejumlah aspek yang perlu diperhitungkan sebelum kebijakan tersebut diterapkan.

Sementara B50 terus berjalan, pengembangan biofuel nasional juga mulai bergerak ke sektor lain. Pemerintah bersama para pemangku kepentingan tengah mematangkan pengembangan Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) atau bioavtur.

Pengembangan SAF menjadi bagian dari upaya memperluas pemanfaatan bahan bakar berbasis sumber terbarukan ke sektor penerbangan. Dengan demikian, agenda biofuel Indonesia tidak hanya bertumpu pada peningkatan mandatori biodiesel untuk transportasi darat, tetapi juga mulai diarahkan pada diversifikasi pemanfaatannya di sektor energi lainnya.

text:
As ICAO strengthens the global framework for aviation decarbonisation and CORSIA moves into its mandatory phase from 2027, SAF is emerging as a critical pathway for international aviation to achieve measurable emissions reductions. The growing adoption of SAF, supported by global frameworks, national mandates and industry action, will be central to accelerating aviation’s transition towards net-zero.

As a recent development, the Ministry of Civil Aviation reviewed India’s preparedness for SAF adoption and compliance with the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA), reaffirming the government’s strong support for building a robust SAF ecosystem. The focus on SAF production, supply-chain development, certification, traceability, and carbon accounting demonstrates India’s readiness to accelerate SAF deployment ahead of CORSIA’s mandatory phase from 1 January 2027.

ICAO has set a global aspirational vision for SAF and other cleaner aviation energies to deliver a 5% reduction in international aviation CO₂ emissions by 2030, while countries are developing national SAF blending targets to support this goal. India’s indicative SAF blending targets for international flights are 1% in 2027, 2% in 2028 and 5% by 2030. A 5% blend is estimated to require approximately 0.4–0.5 million tonnes of SAF annually. Based on ICAO lifecycle values, UCO-based HEFA SAF can achieve an estimated 84% lifecycle emissions reduction compared with conventional jet fuel; At a 5% SAF blend by 2030, India could achieve an estimated 4.2% lifecycle CO₂ emissions reduction versus conventional jet fuel, assuming the SAF is produced through the UCO-based HEFA pathway.

UCO alone cannot meet India’s SAF needs. Feedstocks such as crop residues, bagasse, municipal waste, waste fats and oils, sustainable oilseeds and PtL can diversify supply and support farmer incomes. Agricultural-residue SAF could generate an estimated US$50+ million for around 300,000 farmers, supported by initiatives such as the Pradhan Mantri JI-VAN Yojana.

Beyond SAF, greater formalisation of UCO collection could support energy security, the circular bioeconomy, responsible waste management and livelihoods. A policy assessment has indicated potential annual import savings of ₹20,000–30,000 crore, industry value creation of ₹10,000-20,000 crore and possible public-health savings of ₹50,000–80,000 crore, subject to further techno-economic assessment.

The SAF Association has proposed a Used Cooking Oil Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework to relevant government stakeholders, covering mandatory collection targets, EPR certificates linked to verified recovery, registration of collectors and aggregators, digital traceability and recognition of the last-mile collection workforce. The objective is to build a transparent and traceable supply chain from kitchen and farm to refinery and certified SAF production.

Rohit Kumar, Secretary General, SAF Association and CMAI, said:

“India is not short of feedstock; the opportunity is to build systems that can responsibly collect, verify and bring these resources into the SAF value chain. Feedstock mobilisation deserves the same attention as technology, finance and offtake.”

Manish Marwaha, Founder & CEO, Byufuel, said:

“India’s SAF programme will depend not only on technology, but on building credible and traceable feedstock supply chains. Connecting the kitchen and farm to the refinery can unlock important domestic resources for India’s SAF transition.”

Byufuel currently collects UCO from food businesses across 70+ Indian cities and supplies it to refineries through certified supply chains supported by digital chain-of-custody systems.

A National Conversation with a Global Audience

These issues will be addressed at the 2nd India SAF Conclave & Awards 2026, on 28–29 September 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, under the theme “Powering the SAF Transition Together.” The Conclave will bring together 25+ countries, 1,000+ delegates and 100+ speakers, including policymakers, airlines, SAF producers, refiners, technology providers, feedstock companies, investors and international institutions, with discussions spanning feedstock, technology, sustainability, offtake, finance, CORSIA, certification and international partnerships.

The SAF Association

The SAF Association (SAFA) is India’s leading not-for-profit industry body dedicated exclusively to advancing the Sustainable Aviation Fuel ecosystem through policy advocacy, industry collaboration, international partnerships, technology development, market development and capacity building.

title: [Artigo] O Brasil tem uma Lei que disciplina seu futuro para os biocombustíveis
description:
Enquanto as nações buscavam fontes alternativas de energia, eis que o Brasil desponta, em 1975, com uma proposta pioneira em termos de descarbonização: o Proálcool.
Economia de 3,3 bilhões de barris de petróleo, algo em torno de 35% de toda a reserva do pré-sal.
O Brasil economizou, com os biocombustíveis, aproximadamente US$ 350 bilhões, montante equivalente às reservas cambiais do País no ano de 2025.
Isso é possível porque a cadeia dos biocombustíveis é extensa, altamente integrada, possuindo interfaces estratégicas com diversas outras cadeias produtivas.
O que faltava era previsibilidade regulatória para orientar investimentos privados, decisões industriais e políticas públicas de médio e longo prazo.
text:
Há uma história por trás. O ano era 1973 e o mundo estava em meio a uma crise sem precedentes, com o preço do petróleo indo às alturas por causa da Guerra do Yom Kippur e do embargo da OPEP (Organização dos Produtores de Petróleo). Enquanto as nações buscavam fontes alternativas de energia, eis que o Brasil desponta, em 1975, com uma proposta pioneira em termos de descarbonização: o Proálcool.

Começava assim o maior e mais bem-sucedido programa de substituição de combustíveis fósseis veiculares do planeta. Em 2004, a criação do PNPB (Programa Nacional de Produção e Uso do Biodiesel) deu os contornos finais ao que se transformou em uma verdadeira Política de Estado. Uma das suas maiores virtudes certamente foi reunir as melhores mentes, as maiores capacidade, em torno de um propósito, mostrando que somos capazes, sim, de implementarmos ações dessa magnitude para consolidar nossa soberania energética.

Os números dão a dimensão dos impactos dessa estratégia ao longo dos últimos 50 anos. Economia de 3,3 bilhões de barris de petróleo, algo em torno de 35% de toda a reserva do pré-sal. Emissão evitada de 1,4 bilhão de toneladas de CO2 pelo uso de etanol, o que representaria cobrir todo o estado de Pernambuco com vegetação nativa. Envolvimento de quase 300 mil agricultores familiares no PNPB, representando uma transferência de renda estimada em R$ 9 bilhões/ano - o mais importante: de privado para privado. O Brasil economizou, com os biocombustíveis, aproximadamente US$ 350 bilhões, montante equivalente às reservas cambiais do País no ano de 2025.

Não obstante tantas externalidades positivas, percebia-se que a política de biocombustíveis não deveria ser um fim em si mesma, ou limitar-se ao cumprimento de percentual de mistura, mas um instrumento para atingir objetivos maiores, que contribuíssem para o desenvolvimento socioeconômico e tecnológico do Brasil. Por isso aprovamos, faz dois anos, a Lei do Combustível do Futuro, da qual tive a responsabilidade de ser o relator, que extrapola o contexto do setor de combustíveis, buscando conectar política energética, política climática, agrícola e industrial para fomentar o surgimento de novas cadeias produtivas. Ou seja, utilizar os Bicombustíveis como vetor de desenvolvimento nacional.

Isso é possível porque a cadeia dos biocombustíveis é extensa, altamente integrada, possuindo interfaces estratégicas com diversas outras cadeias produtivas. Vamos precisar, por exemplo, desenvolver novas matérias-primas energéticas, transformar resíduos em energia elétrica, conceber novos produtos com base renovável e avançar na produção de fertilizantes verdes. Nessa nova economia, não será suficiente ser renovável; será fundamental produzir com uma pegada de carbono cada vez maior. Tudo isso demandará ciência, inovação e tecnologia – um investimento que pode catapultar nosso crescimento.

Segundo a Abiove (Associação Brasileira das Indústrias de Óleos Vegetais), a implementação da lei trará, até 2035, investimento vultoso para o setor, algo em torno de R$ 65,5 bilhões em novas unidades de esmagamento, produção e distribuição de biodiesel, bem como para o fortalecimento da cadeia do farelo e ração animal. Estima-se a geração de 1,65 milhão de empregos diretos e indiretos em toda a cadeia da soja.

Números igualmente impactantes são esperados para o setor de biometano, que espera mobilizar R$ 216 bilhões em investimentos privados até 2035. Se considerarmos a resposta positiva do setor ao ambiente regulatório criado pela lei – 15 novas plantas em 2 anos –, o biometano caminha a passos largos para ser a nova fronteira dos biocombustíveis. Isso sem falar no fomento de novas rotas tecnológicas, como o SAF (Sustainable Aviation Fuel), o Diesel Verde, os Combustíveis sintéticos, e das tecnologias de remoção e armazenamento de Co2, que podem reduzir cada vez mais a pegada de carbono da economia como um todo.

Em janeiro de 2026, sob minha coordenação, e com o objetivo de fortalecer o papel dos biocombustíveis como vetor estratégico, constituímos a Coalizão Combustível do Futuro, da qual participam entidades do setor produtivo, destacadamente Abihv, Abiogás, Abiove, Abrema, Aprobio, Bioenergia Brasil, Ubrabio, Unem e Única. O monitoramento deste trabalho está sendo feito em parceria com o Monitor Energia do Futuro, cujas informações possibilitarão a identificação de oportunidades com potencial de crescimento e de desenvolvimento tecnológico.

O Brasil já dispõe de uma base agrícola e industrial consolidada, marcada, ao longo das últimas décadas, por ganhos contínuos de produtividade e custos marginais relativamente baixos em relação aos concorrentes internacionais. O que faltava era previsibilidade regulatória para orientar investimentos privados, decisões industriais e políticas públicas de médio e longo prazo.

Ao adotar uma abordagem verdadeiramente sistêmica, integrando políticas voltadas à energia, à indústria, à logística e à agropecuária, a Lei do Combustível do Futuro consolida os biocombustíveis como um pilar para a construção de um projeto nacional de desenvolvimento sustentável.

Arnaldo Jardim é deputado federal e presidente da Comissão Especial de Transição Energética da Câmara dos Deputados

title: India's SAF Push: 94 percent of UCO Remains Uncollected - The Tribune
description:
VMPL New Delhi [India], September 19: As India prepares to scale Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), significant domestic feedstock potential remains outside organised supply chains.
India consumes approximately 29–30 million tonnes of edible oil annually, creating a substantial potential UCO resource for SAF.
India’s indicative SAF blending targets for international flights are 1% in 2027, 2% in 2028 and 5% by 2030.
UCO alone cannot meet India’s SAF needs.
Beyond SAF, greater formalisation of UCO collection could support energy security, the circular bioeconomy, responsible waste management and livelihoods.
text:
VMPL

New Delhi [India], September 19: As India prepares to scale Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF), significant domestic feedstock potential remains outside organised supply chains. India generates an estimated 1.8–2.6 million tonnes of Used Cooking Oil (UCO) annually, but only around 110,000–156,000 tonnes, or approximately 6%, is formally collected, leaving nearly 94% uncollected. India consumes approximately 29–30 million tonnes of edible oil annually, creating a substantial potential UCO resource for SAF.

As ICAO strengthens the global framework for aviation decarbonisation and CORSIA moves into its mandatory phase from 2027, SAF is emerging as a critical pathway for international aviation to achieve measurable emissions reductions. The growing adoption of SAF, supported by global frameworks, national mandates and industry action, will be central to accelerating aviation’s transition towards net-zero.

As a recent development, the Ministry of Civil Aviation reviewed India’s preparedness for SAF adoption and compliance with the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA), reaffirming the government's strong support for building a robust SAF ecosystem. The focus on SAF production, supply-chain development, certification, traceability, and carbon accounting demonstrates India’s readiness to accelerate SAF deployment ahead of CORSIA’s mandatory phase from 1 January 2027.

ICAO has set a global aspirational vision for SAF and other cleaner aviation energies to deliver a 5% reduction in international aviation CO₂ emissions by 2030, while countries are developing national SAF blending targets to support this goal. India’s indicative SAF blending targets for international flights are 1% in 2027, 2% in 2028 and 5% by 2030. A 5% blend is estimated to require approximately 0.4–0.5 million tonnes of SAF annually. Based on ICAO lifecycle values, UCO-based HEFA SAF can achieve an estimated 84% lifecycle emissions reduction compared with conventional jet fuel; At a 5% SAF blend by 2030, India could achieve an estimated 4.2% lifecycle CO₂ emissions reduction versus conventional jet fuel, assuming the SAF is produced through the UCO-based HEFA pathway.

UCO alone cannot meet India’s SAF needs. Feedstocks such as crop residues, bagasse, municipal waste, waste fats and oils, sustainable oilseeds and PtL can diversify supply and support farmer incomes. Agricultural-residue SAF could generate an estimated US$50+ million for around 300,000 farmers, supported by initiatives such as the Pradhan Mantri JI-VAN Yojana.

Beyond SAF, greater formalisation of UCO collection could support energy security, the circular bioeconomy, responsible waste management and livelihoods. A policy assessment has indicated potential annual import savings of ₹20,000–30,000 crore, industry value creation of ₹10,000-20,000 crore and possible public-health savings of ₹50,000–80,000 crore, subject to further techno-economic assessment.

The SAF Association has proposed a Used Cooking Oil Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework to relevant government stakeholders, covering mandatory collection targets, EPR certificates linked to verified recovery, registration of collectors and aggregators, digital traceability and recognition of the last-mile collection workforce. The objective is to build a transparent and traceable supply chain from kitchen and farm to refinery and certified SAF production.

Rohit Kumar, Secretary General, SAF Association and CMAI, said:

“India is not short of feedstock; the opportunity is to build systems that can responsibly collect, verify and bring these resources into the SAF value chain. Feedstock mobilisation deserves the same attention as technology, finance and offtake.”

Manish Marwaha, Founder & CEO, Byufuel, said:

“India’s SAF programme will depend not only on technology, but on building credible and traceable feedstock supply chains. Connecting the kitchen and farm to the refinery can unlock important domestic resources for India’s SAF transition.”

Byufuel currently collects UCO from food businesses across 70+ Indian cities and supplies it to refineries through certified supply chains supported by digital chain-of-custody systems.

A National Conversation with a Global Audience

These issues will be addressed at the 2nd India SAF Conclave & Awards 2026, on 28–29 September 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, under the theme “Powering the SAF Transition Together.” The Conclave will bring together 25+ countries, 1,000+ delegates and 100+ speakers, including policymakers, airlines, SAF producers, refiners, technology providers, feedstock companies, investors and international institutions, with discussions spanning feedstock, technology, sustainability, offtake, finance, CORSIA, certification and international partnerships.

The SAF Association

The SAF Association (SAFA) is India’s leading not-for-profit industry body dedicated exclusively to advancing the Sustainable Aviation Fuel ecosystem through policy advocacy, industry collaboration, international partnerships, technology development, market development and capacity building.

text:
NINGBO, China--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Allied Biofuels has held a major Front-End Engineering Design (FEED) meeting at Sinopec’s office in Ningbo, China, bringing together Allied Biofuels, Sinopec Engineering Group Co., Ltd. of China, Topsoe A/S of Denmark, Sasol South Africa Limited, and Plug Power of the United States — the principal international engineering and technology providers supporting its US$6.1 billion Presidential Decree-backed Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) and e-SAF project in Uzbekistan.

At the joint FEED meeting of the project’s core engineering and technology stakeholders, the discussions established clear alignment on engineering responsibilities, technology interfaces, design deliverables, project integration and the coordinated execution programme required to advance the project through FEED.

All stakeholders working on the project expressed full confidence in the execution programme and in achieving Final Investment Decision (FID) in Q1 2027.

Sinopec Engineering Group Co., Ltd. of China is delivering FEED, systems integration, Detailed Engineering and open-book cost development, with the project structured for rollover to EPC.

Topsoe A/S of Denmark and Sasol South Africa Limited are providing the core technology license, engineering design package and technical services for the e-SAF production pathway, combining Topsoe’s SynCOR™ technology with Sasol’s Fischer-Tropsch technology.

Plug Power of the United States, through Plug Power Europe SAS, is supporting the project with up to 2.4 GW of GenEco PEM electrolyzer systems, along with the Basic Engineering Design Package and associated engineering services.

These engineering and technology providers bring the world-class technical capability, proven expertise and execution strength required to advance the project through FEED and into the next stage of delivery, with all major workstreams firmly aligned toward achieving FID in Q1 2027.

Alfred Benedict, Managing Director of Allied Biofuels, said:

“The Ningbo meeting confirms the strength of this project and the confidence shared by every stakeholder involved. Sinopec, Topsoe, Sasol and Plug Power are working alongside Allied Biofuels with a common objective, and the engineering and technology workstreams are firmly aligned for execution.

"The responsibilities are clear, the key technology interfaces are aligned and the execution programme is established. All stakeholders have demonstrated full confidence in the project, and we are fully confident in achieving Final Investment Decision in Q1 2027.

"The capability, commitment and alignment demonstrated in Ningbo reinforce our confidence in delivering this project at world scale.”

The Ningbo FEED meeting represents a major milestone in Allied Biofuels’ development programme. It has brought the project’s principal engineering and technology providers into clear alignment on execution and established the coordinated programme required to advance through FEED.

Allied Biofuels and all stakeholders working on the project are proceeding with full confidence toward Final Investment Decision in Q1 2027.

About Allied Biofuels

Allied Biofuels is developing Central Asia’s first world-scale integrated biorefinery in Uzbekistan, purpose-engineered for the industrial-scale production of Sustainable Aviation Fuel and e-SAF.

The US$6.1 billion Presidential Decree-backed development integrates advanced fuels technology, renewable energy, green hydrogen production, international engineering expertise and a global commercial and logistics platform.

Working with leading international engineering and technology providers, Allied Biofuels is developing a world-scale sustainable aviation fuels project designed to establish Uzbekistan as a significant future producer and supplier to the global aviation market.

title: B50, E5, dan E10: Jalan Baru Kedaulatan Energi dan Kewirausahaan Hijau - Investor Daily
description:
E5 dan E10: Membangun Ekosistem, Bukan Sekadar Mandatori Jika B50 menjadi jawaban terhadap ketergantungan impor solar, maka E5 dan E10 merupakan bagian dari jawaban terhadap ketergantungan impor bensin.
Dengan desain tersebut, E5 dan E10 tidak berubah menjadi pasar baru bagi produk impor, tetapi menjadi fondasi industrialisasi bioetanol nasional.
Karena itu, saya mengajak generasi muda Indonesia untuk tidak sekadar menjadi penonton dalam transformasi ini.
Jika generasi muda berani masuk sejak sekarang, Indonesia bukan hanya akan menjadi pasar energi hijau, tetapi juga pusat inovasi, produksi, dan kewirausahaan bioenergi dunia.
Pada akhirnya, B50, E5, dan E10 bukan sekadar persoalan mencampurkan bahan bakar nabati ke dalam bahan bakar fosil.
text:
E5 dan E10: Membangun Ekosistem, Bukan Sekadar Mandatori

Jika B50 menjadi jawaban terhadap ketergantungan impor solar, maka E5 dan E10 merupakan bagian dari jawaban terhadap ketergantungan impor bensin.

E5 merupakan campuran 5 persen bioetanol dengan 95 persen bensin, sedangkan E10 mengandung 10 persen bioetanol. Secara teknis, konsepnya terlihat sederhana. Namun, kesiapan ekosistem bioetanol Indonesia masih berbeda jauh dibandingkan industri biodiesel.

Industri biodiesel ditopang oleh perkebunan sawit dan kapasitas pengolahan yang relatif matang. Sementara itu, bioetanol masih menghadapi keterbatasan bahan baku, kapasitas produksi, kepastian pasar, formula harga, fasilitas pencampuran, dan infrastruktur distribusi.

Karena itu, E5 tidak boleh dipandang hanya sebagai kewajiban mencampurkan etanol ke dalam bensin. E5 harus ditempatkan sebagai fase awal pembangunan pasar. Pemerintah perlu memberikan kepastian permintaan agar investor berani membangun pabrik, lembaga pembiayaan bersedia masuk, petani meningkatkan produksi, dan distributor bahan bakar menyiapkan infrastruktur.

ADVERTISEMENT

Implementasinya dapat dilakukan secara bertahap pada wilayah yang dekat dengan sentra bahan baku, fasilitas produksi, dan titik pencampuran. Setelah pasokan, mutu, harga, dan distribusinya stabil, cakupan E5 dapat diperluas sebelum Indonesia meningkatkan bauran menuju E10.

Sumber bahan baku juga tidak boleh bergantung pada satu komoditas. Tebu tetap penting, tetapi Indonesia perlu mengembangkan etanol berbasis molase, singkong, sorgum, jagung sesuai daya dukung wilayah, serta secara bertahap mengembangkan etanol generasi kedua dari limbah lignoselulosa.

Prinsipnya jelas: kebijakan energi tidak boleh menimbulkan kompetisi yang tidak sehat dengan pangan. Setiap kawasan harus memiliki peta jalan bahan baku berdasarkan produktivitas, ketersediaan air, karakteristik lahan, efisiensi logistik, dan pengaruhnya terhadap kebutuhan pangan masyarakat.

Dalam tahap awal, relaksasi impor etanol secara terbatas dapat dipertimbangkan sebagai jembatan untuk membuka pasar dan membangun permintaan. Namun, kebijakan tersebut harus memiliki batas waktu, volume, dan peta jalan substitusi yang jelas.

Impor tidak boleh menjadi tujuan akhir. Relaksasi harus menjadi sweetener untuk menarik investasi pabrik bioetanol di dalam negeri. Insentif dapat dikaitkan dengan realisasi investasi, pembangunan kapasitas produksi, kemitraan dengan petani, penggunaan bahan baku domestik, dan transfer teknologi.

Dengan desain tersebut, E5 dan E10 tidak berubah menjadi pasar baru bagi produk impor, tetapi menjadi fondasi industrialisasi bioetanol nasional.

Belajar dari Brasil tanpa Menyalin Mentah-Mentah

Brasil membuktikan bahwa bioetanol dapat berkembang apabila didukung konsistensi kebijakan selama puluhan tahun. Industri otomotifnya membangun kendaraan flex-fuel, konsumen memperoleh pilihan, sementara jaringan distribusi berkembang bersama industri bahan baku.

Indonesia dapat mengambil pelajaran dari keberhasilan tersebut tanpa harus menyalin seluruh modelnya. Struktur pertanian, kondisi geografis, daya beli konsumen, kapasitas fiskal, dan karakteristik industri Indonesia berbeda.

Hal yang perlu ditiru adalah konsistensi kebijakannya. Investor bukan hanya membutuhkan insentif fiskal, tetapi juga kepastian mengenai target bauran, volume penyerapan, mekanisme harga, standar mutu, lokasi pengembangan, serta pembagian risiko antara pemerintah dan dunia usaha.

Indonesia juga perlu memiliki satu peta jalan biofuel nasional yang menyatukan biodiesel, bioetanol, bioavtur, biogas, bio-CNG, biomassa, dan bahan bakar nabati generasi berikutnya. Berbagai program tersebut tidak dapat terus berjalan sendiri-sendiri karena menggunakan sumber daya lahan, bahan baku, dana insentif, infrastruktur, dan pasar energi yang saling berkaitan.

Ruang Besar bagi Generasi Muda

Transformasi bioenergi tidak boleh hanya menjadi agenda pemerintah dan perusahaan besar. Sektor ini harus menjadi ruang baru bagi generasi muda, pengusaha pemula, mahasiswa, peneliti, serta pelaku UMKM untuk membangun usaha dan menciptakan inovasi.

Peluangnya sangat luas dan tidak terbatas pada pembangunan pabrik biodiesel atau bioetanol. Generasi muda dapat masuk melalui teknologi pengolahan biomassa, pengumpulan dan pemurnian minyak jelantah, produksi biogas dan bio-CNG, pengolahan limbah sawit menjadi energi, produksi pelet biomassa, perdagangan karbon, penyediaan alat dan komponen, laboratorium pengujian, logistik bahan baku, digitalisasi rantai pasok, hingga jasa konsultasi keberlanjutan dan keterlacakan produk.

Indonesia memiliki sumber daya bioenergi yang tersebar dari desa hingga kawasan industri. Tandan kosong sawit, limbah cair kelapa sawit atau POME, jerami, sekam padi, tongkol jagung, ampas tebu, limbah peternakan, sampah organik, dan minyak jelantah dapat diubah dari beban lingkungan menjadi produk ekonomi.

Di sinilah kreativitas dan keberanian generasi muda dibutuhkan: mengubah limbah menjadi energi, persoalan lingkungan menjadi solusi, serta potensi daerah menjadi usaha yang menciptakan pekerjaan.

Pasar bioenergi tidak hanya terbentuk karena kewajiban pemerintah. Permintaan akan terus berkembang dari industri yang ingin mengurangi emisi, sektor transportasi dan penerbangan, kawasan industri hijau, perusahaan yang memiliki target keberlanjutan, hingga pasar ekspor.

Perkembangan biodiesel, bioetanol, sustainable aviation fuel, biomassa, biogas, dan bio-CNG akan melahirkan rantai nilai, profesi, dan model bisnis baru yang belum banyak digarap.

Generasi muda jangan hanya menjadi pedagang yang menikmati momentum sesaat. Mereka harus masuk sebagai inovator, produsen, pengembang teknologi, serta pemilik kekayaan intelektual. Jangan sekadar menjual kembali produk yang sudah ada, tetapi menciptakan mesin, aplikasi, proses produksi, sistem logistik, dan solusi baru yang dapat dikembangkan dari Indonesia ke pasar dunia.

Kampus harus menjadi pusat riset sekaligus inkubasi usaha bioenergi. Industri perlu membuka ruang kemitraan, magang, riset terapan, serta proyek percontohan. Sementara itu, pemerintah perlu menyediakan kepastian regulasi, akses pembiayaan, fasilitas pengujian, perlindungan kekayaan intelektual, dan skema pengadaan yang memberi kesempatan kepada perusahaan rintisan.

Bioenergi mempertemukan tiga kebutuhan besar sekaligus: ketahanan energi, penciptaan lapangan kerja, dan pelestarian lingkungan. Karena itu, saya mengajak generasi muda Indonesia untuk tidak sekadar menjadi penonton dalam transformasi ini.

Jangan hanya bertanya di mana pekerjaan tersedia. Mulailah bertanya: persoalan energi apa yang dapat kita selesaikan dan bisnis apa yang dapat kita bangun?

B50, E5, dan E10 hanyalah pintu masuk. Di belakangnya terbentang ekosistem bioenergi yang jauh lebih luas. Jika generasi muda berani masuk sejak sekarang, Indonesia bukan hanya akan menjadi pasar energi hijau, tetapi juga pusat inovasi, produksi, dan kewirausahaan bioenergi dunia.

Pada akhirnya, B50, E5, dan E10 bukan sekadar persoalan mencampurkan bahan bakar nabati ke dalam bahan bakar fosil. Ketiganya merupakan instrumen untuk mengubah kekuatan pertanian menjadi kekuatan energi, industri, inovasi, dan geopolitik.

Indonesia tidak boleh puas hanya menjadi produsen minyak sawit, tebu, singkong, atau biomassa. Kita harus mengolah kekayaan tersebut menjadi energi, teknologi, lapangan kerja, dan nilai tambah di dalam negeri.

B50 adalah momentum konsolidasi. E5 adalah pintu masuk. E10 adalah tahap penguatan. Generasi muda adalah penggeraknya. Tujuan akhirnya adalah membangun kedaulatan energi yang produktif, terjangkau, berkelanjutan, dan berpihak kepada kepentingan nasional.

The partnership highlights JAL’s continued commitment to supporting CORSIA and advancing the use of high-integrity carbon removal technologies.
